title: How close is the Trump administration to the toxic Tate brothers? Let’s ask the president’s son Barron … | Arwa Mahdawi | The Guardian
description: The 20-year-old crypto bro likes to keep a low profile. He could still be forced to testify before the House oversight committee, writes Arwa Mahdawi
Author: Arwa Mahdawi
Headline: The 20-year-old crypto bro likes to keep a low profile. He could still be forced to testify before the House oversight committee, writes Arwa Mahdawi
Content: ‘Barron is a full-blown adult and very influential in the Trump White House orbit.’Photograph: Carlos Barría/ReutersView image in fullscreen‘Barron is a full-blown adult and very influential in the Trump White House orbit.’Photograph: Carlos Barría/ReutersOpinionAndrew TateHow close is the Trump administration to the toxic Tate brothers? Let’s ask the president’s son Barron …Arwa MahdawiThe 20-year-old crypto bro likes to keep a low profile. He could still be forced to testify before the House oversight committeeTue 28 Jul 2026 09.59 EDTLast modified on Tue 28 Jul 2026 14.30 EDTShareUnlike his garrulous father, Barron Trump seems to be a man of few words. The president’s youngest son has been busy floggingenergy drinksand making millions from cryptocurrency schemes, but he’s not big on public speaking. Indeed, the best-known clip of him talking is probably from when he was four years old and said “I like my suitcase” in aSlovenian accent.Still, while 20-year-old Barron Trump might prefer to stay behind the scenes, he may find himself hauled in front of Congress and forced to answer some difficult questions. Last week,Yassamin Ansari, a Democratic congresswoman and a member of the House oversight committee,called forBarron to testify about his alleged connections to the toxic influencers Andrew and Tristan Tate. The Tate brothers, who have become household names by monetising misogyny, wererecently arrestedin Miami, just before Andrew was due to co-host a bare-knuckle boxing event. They’re nowfighting extraditionto the UK, and face allegations of rape, assault, trafficking and offences relating to “indecent images of a child and extreme pornography”. They deny these charges.What’s Barron got to do with all this? Over the years, the Trumps and the Tates seem to have forged a mutually beneficial alliance. Donald Trump Jr has been friendly with Andrewsince 2016and, while I wouldn’t go so far as to call Barron and Andrew besties, theNew York Times has reportedthat a teenage Barron admired the influencer and had a Zoom call with him. Accordingto the New Yorker, Barron also spent a lot of time with Justin Waller, who has called himself the Tates’ “third brother”, and gave Barrondating advice. Barron, in turn, gave his dad a political steer: he is widely credited, including by thepresident himself, for pushing Trump to tap into manosphere influencers such as Tate during the 2024 election in order to mobilise young male voters.In return for their help with the election, the Tates got friends in high places. “The Tates will be free, Trump is the president,”Andrew postedafter the inauguration. And that prediction was partly correct: it has beenwidelyreportedthat the Trump administration intervened in 2025 to get the Romanian governmentto lift travel restrictionson the Tates, who were under house arrest in the country for trafficking charges. (Romania’s foreign minister has said he did not face any pressure from the US regarding the Tates. The Trump administration has said it had no insight into the matter.)Will the Trump administration help the brothers when it comes to this new extradition request? Press secretary Karoline Leavitt has said the White Housewon’t get involved. Secretary of state Marco Rubio has alsodismissed the idea. Whether you should believe this is debatable, but it’s certainly possible the Tates have outlived their usefulness to the ever-transactional Trumps.Still, the Trump family can’t sever ties with the Tate brothers that easily. As congresswoman Ansari notes, there are plenty of questions that remain unanswered about the Tate-Trump relationship. Ina letterto the House oversight committee chair, Ansari said: “The committee must investigate whether back-channel communications between the Tate brothers, presidential advisors, and members of the First Family such as Barron Trump influenced official actions or administration policy regarding criminal prosecution and investigation of the brothers or international law enforcement cooperation.” The letter specifically recommends a subpoena for Barron to see if he had “any involvement” in relation to the Tate brothers’ allegedcrimes. Over the weekend,Ansari reiterated her callsfor an investigation on the MeidasTouchpodcast, noting that Barron “is a full-blown adult, and he is very influential in the Trump White House orbit”.Staff turnover is rampant under Trump 2.0 – with insidious results | Arwa MahdawiRead moreRepublicans have a slight majority in the House, so it’s highly unlikely that Ansari’s request will go anywhere. I don’t need to tell you that we still don’t have real answers about Trump’s ties to Jeffrey Epstein. Nor do I need to tell you that Trump is an adjudicated sexual abuser. This isn’t an administration that takes violence against women seriously. That said, if the Democrats win the House in the midterms, as they areexpected to do, the situation might shift and Barron might find himself with some explaining to do.And if the US government won’t demand answers from Barron, then the media should. As Ansari notes, Barron is very much an adult now. He may not have chosen to be born a Trump but he haschosen to profitfrom his name and connections. He’s not some little kid who needs protecting. But there are a lot ofvulnerable young kidsout there who do need protecting from the bigotry and hate that men like the Tates peddle.Arwa Mahdawi is a Guardian columnistDo you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? If you would like to submit a response of up to 300 words by email to be considered for publication in ourletterssection, pleaseclick hereExplore more on these topicsAndrew TateOpinionTrump administrationUS politicsViolence against women and girlsCrimeCryptocurrenciescommentShareReuse this content

title: Who dares ridicule Gianni Infantino as the World Cup boss creates global peace? Not me: is it you?  | Marina Hyde | The Guardian
description: If you thought he was just a shady rule-dodging reprobate, the Fifa boss’s latest 15-page Instagram rant might make you think again, says Guardian columnist Marina Hyde
Author: Marina Hyde
Headline: If you thought he was just a shady rule-dodging reprobate, the Fifa boss’s latest 15-page Instagram rant might make you think again, says Guardian columnist Marina Hyde
Content: Gianni Infantino and Donald Trump at the World Cup final at the MetLife Stadium in New Jersey on 19 July 2026.Photograph: Bradley Collyer/PAView image in fullscreenGianni Infantino and Donald Trump at the World Cup final at the MetLife Stadium in New Jersey on 19 July 2026.Photograph: Bradley Collyer/PAOpinionGianni InfantinoWho dares ridicule Gianni Infantino as the World Cup boss creates global peace? Not me: is it you?Marina HydeIf you thought he was just a shady rule-dodging reprobate, the Fifa boss’s latest 15-page Instagram rant might make you think againTue 28 Jul 2026 07.42 EDTLast modified on Tue 28 Jul 2026 14.30 EDTShareIhope you have found time to enjoy Fifa president Gianni Infantino’s 15-pageInstagram meltdownabout his World Cup. The last time I saw this many defiant words, they were inked on someone sitting cross-legged on the floor of a Salvadoran supermax prison.Infantino has been clapping back at his haters – putting them on blast, in the parlance of our times – and on this evidence seems mesmerisingly close to picking out a Chicano script font and getting STILL I RISE needled across his corporate clavicles. Right next to the ones reading THROUGH THE FIRE, UNBREAKABLE and BUILT DIFFERENT.“Sorry that the matches are now over and sorry that you missed all that joy and togetherness. Sorry that you were so consumed by hate and criticism that you missed it all,” the Fifa president – reportedly a 56-year-old man – posted yesterday. “To those behind their pens and papers, behind their screens spreading hate and false rumours, I want to say that while you are sitting behind, we at Fifa are on the frontlines organising, working hard, and delivering ‌the best show in the ‌world.” The frontlines of cheating because a fellow presidential shitposter told you to? Hey – it’s a living. Of course, I should say that Infantino denies caving tothe repeated interference from Donald Trumpover the decision to make the red-carded Folarin Balogun available for the US’s last-16 tie. But I see the top Democrat on the House judiciary committee haslaunched an investigation into the Fifa presidentand his ties with the actual president, so ideally Gianni will have the chance to say all this and more in an interview with the committee in due course.But for now, back to his rant. “To those spending their time and energy hating us,” ran a later, time-consumingly energetic section of the Insta-treatise, “please take a moment to reflect, meditate, pray or watch a football match …” Pray? This, takes us firmly into ONLY GOD CAN JUDGE ME territory, with Infantino now presenting as the Tupac of the Switzerland-based sporting governance class.A few years ago I would have said that the Fifa president has forgotten one of the golden rules of modern life – that it’s always fine not to post. You could always, quite simply, just not post. And yet, can that really be said to be the case any more?A fascinating report last week by Luminate, the entertainment data analysts, found that 39% of Americans identified as content creators, whileGoldman Sachs’s own last lookat the subject forecast well over 100 million people globally placing themselves in this class over the next few years.Psychically speaking, Infantino seems to be inching ever-closer to the conviction that he invented the product – football – and that his primary job is not administrating it, but being “out there” on his public channels, forever outlining his philosophy, or stoking geopolitical online beef, or embodying it all in some ineffable, excruciating-to-watch sort of way. In this he shares a kinship with posting megalodons like Elon Musk, as well as tireless minnows like the take-me-back founder of BrewDog,James Watt.Yet the tendency is reflected all the way down the levels of bosses. These days, founders of companies, whom Infantino would no doubt see as his peer group, report being expected to constantly document their thinking publicly and stay permanently visible to attract customers and investors. What was once an optional marketing activity is now a core part of the job, which, for significant chunks of the day, takes them away from such devalued tasks as building the product or running the company. They have discovered, if only subconsciously, that their actual job is posting – that they have to be an always-on personal content creator.In a way football was ahead on all this, as were various other sports. The game’s owners and exploiters have long seen the matches themselves as mere 90-minute sections of legacy content, which would be far better relegated to the second, third or even fourth tier behind such always-on output as branded content, shareable clips, behind-the-scenes footage, lifestyle and commerce.And, of course, viral moments, which is presumably what Infantino was going for with his 15-page algorithm frotting. Here is the promoter as creator – a vibe also embodied by, say,Ultimate Fighting Championships’s Dana White. In fact, in retrospect, Infantino’s main character glow-up been under way for some time. In a mad,hour-long soliloquyahead of the previous World Cup in Qatar, Infantino addressed the world: “You want to criticise someone, come to me. Criticise me. Here I am. Crucify me,” he went on, standing to extend his arms out wide. “Don’t criticise Qatar. Don’t criticise the players. Don’t criticise anyone. Criticise Fifa. Criticise me, if you want. Because I’m responsible for everything.” Fifa itself has long been a supranational body, a travelling parasitic nation-state. But under Infantino, the situation has seemingly evolved into Infantino himself being Fifa. L’état, c’est moi.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toMatters of OpinionGuardian columnists and writers on what they’ve been debating, thinking about, reading, and morePreview latestEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionLet’s play out with another telling passage from his most recent diatribe, in which Infantino announced a diplomatic victory for some reason yet to be meaningfully acknowledged in any sustained way by oil prices. As MrFifaput it: “We worked tirelessly to unite two countries at war”. Is this the US and Iran? OK! I guess someone has to get the Fifa peace prize next year, and what better way to build on the optics triumph of its inaugural recipient than by keeping it in-house, and awarding it to Infantino himself? The first creator-president surely deserves nothing less.Marina Hyde is a Guardian columnistMarina Hyde’s new book, What a Time to be Alive!, is out in September (Guardian Faber Publishing, £20).
