title: Spanish summer recipes: Thomasina Miers’ grilled prawns, red rice and boozy baked peaches | Mexican food and drink | The Guardian
description: An indulgent and satisfying summer lunch: grilled prawns with red rice and allioli; and boozy baked peaches, amaretti biscuits and cold custard for dessert
Author: Thomasina Miers
Headline: An indulgent and satisfying summer lunch: grilled prawns with red rice and allioli; and boozy baked peaches, amaretti biscuits and cold custard for dessert
Content: Thomasina Miers' grilled prawns with red rice and allioli.Photograph: Matthew Hague/The Guardian. Food and prop styling: Florence Blair. Food styling assistant: Phoebe Altman.View image in fullscreenThomasina Miers' grilled prawns with red rice and allioli.Photograph: Matthew Hague/The Guardian. Food and prop styling: Florence Blair. Food styling assistant: Phoebe Altman.Thomasina Miers recipesMexican food and drinkSpanish summer recipes: Thomasina Miers’ grilled prawns, red rice and boozy baked peachesAn indulgent and satisfying summer lunch: grilled prawns with red rice and allioli; and boozy baked peaches, amaretti biscuits and cold custard for dessertThomasina MiersTue 28 Jul 2026 01.00 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleLarge, scented tomatoes are beginning to flood the markets near me, and their presence brings back memories of Mexico. On a trip up north to Ensenada, a famous fishing port, I became obsessed with the Spanish-stylearrozdishes studded with fresh shellfish and seafood of every shape and size. The clams! The crab! On another trip, we sat by the sea for a birthday lunch with the waves crashing on to the sand, while we were presented with a grilled prawnarroz,where the grains were steeped in rich tomato and grilled prawn umami that it was giddying. A cold custard with roast peaches will prolong the fantasy – a lunch that conjures up far away places that you can dream about from home.Grilled prawns with red rice and allioli (pictured top)Want to save this recipe?Download the Guardian Feast app to add this to your collection.Download the appThis may be a showstopper (and deeply delicious), but it is pleasingly straightforward in its execution.Prep10 minCook1 hr 10 minServes4-6400g medium-sized, very ripetomatoes1 redchilli1 redpepper,stem removed100ml olive oil4garlic cloves,peeled; 2 left whole, 2 finely chopped400gprawns,deveined, heads and shells left onSalt and black pepper1 tbsp chipotle en adobo,plus 1 heaped tsp1 tbsp sherry vinegar,plus 1 tsp1 largered onion,peeled and finely chopped½ fennel bulb,finely chopped1 large pinch saffron400g short-grain rice250g good-quality mayonnaise180gfresh or frozenpeasChopped chives or parsley,to garnish (optional)Put a frying pan over a high heat, add the tomatoes, chilli and red pepper, and dry toast, turning occasionally, for 10-12 minutes, until the tomatoes and chilli are blackened all over. Transfer the tomatoes and chilli into an upright blender, and continue to cook the pepper, either directly over a flame or in the pan, until blackened. Put the pepper in a bowl, cover with clingfilm and set aside.Meanwhile, heat a large paella pan or frying pan (preferably with a lid) over a high heat. Once hot, add a few tablespoons of oil and the whole garlic cloves, and cook for a few minutes, until they turn golden around the edges. Add the prawns, season generously and saute for four to five minutes, until colouring on all sides.Make a stock by tearing the prawn heads from the bodies and adding them to the blender with a tablespoon of chipotle and a tablespoon of sherry vinegar. Blitz to a puree, then pour in 500ml boiling water and blend again for 30 seconds. Set the prawns and garlic aside.Pour the remaining oil into the large pan and sweat the onion and fennel over a medium heat for 10 minutes, until translucent, seasoning with salt and pepper. Now add the chopped garlic and saffron, cook for a few minutes, then stir in the rice for a few minutes, until the grains are coated in oil. Pour in the tomato and shrimp stock, taste and add more salt if needed, then cook uncovered over a medium heat for 18 minutes – do not stir!Meanwhile, peel and deseed the pepper and cut it into thin strips. Put a quarter of them into the blender with the mayonnaise, reserved sauteed garlic, and remaining chipotle and sherry vinegar. Blitz and adjust the seasoning.Tip the peas on to the rice and arrange the pepper slices in a fun pattern. Cover and cook for a further 12 minutes either on the stove or in a 200C (180C fan)/390F/gas 6 oven, which gives a more golden result. In the last two or three minutes of cooking, return the prawns to the rice, along with any of their juices – again, don’t stir.Serve the rice at the table garnished with the herbs, plus the allioli on the side and a crisp, green salad.Baked peaches, amaretti and cold custardWant to save this recipe?Download the Guardian Feast app to add this to your collection.Download the appView image in fullscreenPrep10 minChillovernightCook1 hrServes66 large, ripe peaches,cut in half and stones removed100mlchardonnay orcheninblanc4tbsp soft brown sugar½ tsp green cardamom seeds,finely ground6 amaretti biscuits(optional)For the custard600ml double cream1 vanilla pod,cut in half and seeds scraped out, or 1 tsp vanilla extract3 eggs, plus 1 egg yolk60g unrefined caster sugar1tbspamarettoTo make the custard, put the cream, vanilla pod and seeds (or vanilla extract) into a saucepan over a medium heat and heat until the cream is shimmering but not yet boiling. Take off the heat and leave to infuse.Meanwhile, whisk the eggs and yolk in a bowl with the caster sugar, until light and fluffy, then whisk in the amaretto. Pour the infused cream into the eggs, whisking as you do, then pour back into the pan over a low heat. Stir with a wooden spoon until the cream reaches 88C on a thermometer, then remove from the heat. Pour the mix through a fine sieve into a clean bowl and leave to cool for 10-15 minutes. Finally, using a stick blender, blend until smooth, pour into individual glasses or bowls and leave overnight in the fridge to set.The next day, heat the oven to 220C (200C fan)/425F/gas 7. Arrange the peaches cut side up in a roasting tin pour over the wine and sprinkle over the sugar and cardamom, and roast for 20-25 minutes, until the peaches are golden. Serve the peaches with the cold custard, a splash more amaretto poured over and a few biscuits crumbled on top, if you like.Explore more on these topicsMexican food and drinkThomasina Miers recipesFoodShellfishSeafoodRiceTomatoesFruitrecipesShareReuse this content

title: Scoop of the year! We taste-test 99 of 2026’s most unusual ice creams, from the unbeatable to the unlickable | Ice-cream and sorbet | The Guardian
description: From olive oil to matcha, soy sauce to sage and onion stuffing, there’s a frozen designer dessert out there to tickle even the most jaded palate. Here’s the best – and worst – of what’s on offer in Britain this summer
Author: Lucy Knight
Headline: From olive oil to matcha, soy sauce to sage and onion stuffing, there’s a frozen designer dessert out there to tickle even the most jaded palate. Here’s the best – and worst – of what’s on offer in Britain this summer
Content: Lucy Knight on her mammoth taste test.Photograph: Alicia Canter/The GuardianView image in fullscreenLucy Knight on her mammoth taste test.Photograph: Alicia Canter/The GuardianTaste testIce-cream and sorbetScoop of the year! We taste-test 99 of 2026’s most unusual ice creams, from the unbeatable to the unlickableFrom olive oil to matcha, soy sauce to sage and onion stuffing, there’s a frozen designer dessert out there to tickle even the most jaded palate. Here’s the best – and worst – of what’s on offer in Britain this summerLucy KnightTue 28 Jul 2026 00.00 EDTLast modified on Tue 28 Jul 2026 09.04 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleWhat’s with all the weird ice-cream flavours this year? It feels as if supermarkets and independent companies are vying to make the most novel alternatives to a good old scoop of vanilla. But which are actually worth having? I tried 99 varieties of ice-cream tubs and ranked them from sickeningly sweet to dinner party-worthy.99.Paxo sage and onion stuffing,Anya Hindmarch(One scoop £4.50 or 500ml tub £16, The Ice Cream Project, London)Anya Hindmarch’s Ice Cream Project has become a yearly summer fixture, in which the fashion designer collaborates with well-known brands to create nostalgic novelty flavours (at designer prices) for which customers queue round the block. This year the flavours skew toward roast dinners, and include Oxo (which I couldn’t try, being vegetarian) and Paxo. It tastes exactly like the stuffing … which isn’t really what I want from an ice-cream.Taste 1/10, Value 1/10, Originality 7/10View image in fullscreen‘It tastes exactly like the stuffing’.Photograph: PR98.Highproteinchocolatebrownie, Oppo(240ml, £3.50, Ocado)A disgraceful, claggy, protein bar-flavoured excuse for an ice-cream.Taste 1/10, Value 5/10, Originality 4/1097.Crunchie, Cadbury(425ml, £4.02, Asda)Sickly sweet; very, very orange in colour, with a weird, foamy, almost mousse-like texture.Taste 3/10, Value 5/10, Originality 2/1096.Hobnobs, McVitie’s(500ml, £4, Iceland)Grainy and overly sweet. Hobnob fans should stay away and avoid disappointment.Taste 3/10, Value 5/10, Originality 2/1095.Caramelised biscuit swirl, Oppo(475ml, £5.40, Ocado)This sickly-sweet ice-cream demonstrates exactly why “low-calorie” ice-cream shouldn’t be a thing.Taste 3/10, Value 5/10, Originality 3/1094.Jacob’s Mini Cheddars,Anya Hindmarch(One scoop £4.50 or 500ml tub £16, The Ice Cream Project, London)Cheese ice-cream apparently has a long history in the UK, but this version doesn’t do that history any justice. Slightly coarse texture and familiar Mini Cheddars flavour.Taste 3/10, Value 1/10, Originality 7/1093.Amarena cherry cheesecake, Hackney Gelato(460ml, £5.75, Waitrose)I wanted more cheesiness from this one, too, and a less synthetic cherry flavour.Taste 3/10, Value 5/10, Originality 3/1092.Cherryand mascarpone gelato, Crosta & Mollica(450ml, £4.60, Waitrose)Soft-serve style, prettily swirled in its recyclable box, underdelivers on flavour.Taste 4/10, Value 5/10, Originality 2/1091.Cornish sea salted caramel brittle, No 1 Waitrose(480ml, £4.50, Waitrose)Unlike most salted caramel treats, this was actually well salted, and the brittle was nice and crunchy – even if salted caramel ice-cream feels a bit old hat these days.Taste 4/10, Value 6/10, Originality 1/1090.Strawberry cheesecake,Häagen-Dazs(460ml, £5.75, Tesco)Overly sweet and artificial-tasting.Taste 4/10, Value 5/10, Originality 2/1089.Milk chocolate digestives, McVitie’s(500ml, £4, Iceland)If you’re going to put biscuit pieces in an ice-cream, you need to find a way to stop them going soft. Nobody wants soggy biscuits!Taste 4/10, Value 5/10, Originality 2/1088.Peanut butter and milk chocolate, Reese’s(460ml, £5.50, Iceland)I love Reese’s peanut butter cups, so I had high hopes. But though it had a satisfying crackly chocolate swirl, it was slightly cloying and gritty overall.Taste 5/10, Value 4/10, Originality 2/10View image in fullscreen‘Slightly cloying and gritty’ … Peanut butter and milk chocolate.Photograph: Lucy Knight/The Guardian87.Proteinspeculoos, Jude’s(460ml, £5, Ocado)This vegan, high-protein ice-cream is another soggy biscuit offender, and leaves an almost yeasty aftertaste. Avoid.Taste 2/10, Value 5/10, Originality 4/1086.Colombian coffee, M&S collection(500ml, £4.50, Ocado)The crushed-up coffee beans create a sandy texture which I didn’t love.Taste 5/10, Value 5/10, Originality 1/1085.Green Giant sweetcorn,Anya Hindmarch(One scoop £4.50 or 500ml tub £16, The Ice Cream Project, London)It’s a bold move to put chunks of sweetcorn in an ice-cream, and I’m not sure it pays off.Taste 4/10, Value 1/10, Originality 7/1084.Walker’s shortbread,Anya Hindmarch(One scoop £4.50, 500ml tub £16, The Ice Cream Project, London)The texture was a bit too hard. The sweet-salty flavour was perfectly nice, though.Taste 4/10, Value 1/10, Originality 7/1083.Oreo(425ml, £3.50, Iceland)Spongey texture; slightly nothing-y flavour.Taste 4/10, Value 6/10, Originality 2/1082.Tunnock’s caramel wafers,Anya Hindmarch(One scoop £4.50, 500ml tub £16, The Ice Cream Project, London)Way too sweet!Taste 4/10, Value 1/10, Originality 7/1081.Macadamia nut brittle, Häagen-Dazs(460ml, £5.75, Ocado)Another one that is far too sickly sweet. There was a slight saltiness for balance, but not enough.Taste 5/10, Value 5/10, Originality 2/1080.Nutella(470ml, £5.50, Iceland)It’s fun that this one looks exactly like a jar of Nutella, and you have to break through a layer of Nutella spread to get to the ice-cream. Fans of the spread will love it; it was a bit too intense for me.Taste 5/10, Value 5/10, Originality 2/1079.Soy Joy cookie dough, M&S(320ml, £4, Ocado)This soy ice-cream did not, sadly, bring me joy. It’s cloying and artificial-tasting – there are far better vegan ice-creams out there.Taste 3/10, Value 5/10, Originality 4/10View image in fullscreenLucy Knight prepares to try some of the more offbeat flavours of ice-cream.Photograph: Lucy Knight/The Guardian77-73.Capri-Sun orange / Müller Corner strawberry / McVitie’sgingernuts / Yazoo chocolate milk /Illy coffee,Anya Hindmarch(one scoop £4.50 or 500ml tub £16, The Ice Cream Project, London)These all tasted exactly like the products they’re based on.Taste 5/10, Value 1/10, Originality 7/1072.Piñacolada, Soleya(500ml, £9.50, selected UK stores)There is no alcohol in this rather insipid vegan ice-cream, which is more of a sorbet.Taste 3/10, Value 4/10, Originality 6/1071-70.Chocolate salted caramel / Caramel pecan praline, Booja Booja(465ml, £5.65, Booja Booja)Both of these vegan chocolate ice-creams have an intense chocolatey flavour.Taste 5/10, Value 5/10, Originality 3/1069.Biscoff, Lotus(425ml, £2.50, Iceland)Anyone who has enjoyed spooning Biscoff spread directly into their mouth will be in heaven.Taste 6/10, Value 5/10, Originality 2/1068.Blueberry and lemon curd, Yeo Valley(480ml, £4.75, Ocado)Very strong lemon curd flavour, with chunks of fresh blueberry. This isn’t a flavour combination I love, but I can appreciate that it’s a very good ice-cream.Taste 6/10, Value 5/10, Originality 2/10View image in fullscreen‘A very good ice-cream’ … Blueberry and lemon curd.Photograph: Yeo Valley67.Kikkoman soy sauce,Anya Hindmarch(one scoop £4.50 or 500ml tub £16, The Ice Cream Project, London)I loved the salty first spoonful of this – but any more than that becomes overwhelming.Taste 5/10, Value 1/10, Originality 7/1066.Rhubarbandcustard, Waitrose(480ml, £3.50, Waitrose)Pure nostalgia!Taste 3/10, Value 7/10, Originality 4/1065.Lurpak salted butter,Anya Hindmarch(one scoop £4.50 or 500ml tub £16, The Ice Cream Project, London)Lovely and creamy, but could have been saltier.Taste 6/10, Value 1/10, Originality 7/1064.Vanilla andblackcardamom, Moonji(100ml, £3.49, selected UK stores and online)I wanted more cardamom from this plant-based ice-cream.Taste 5/10, Value 3/10, Originality 6/1063.Millionaires shortbread with cornish clotted cream, Kelly’s(425ml, £4, Iceland)Crunchy chunks of chocolate and biscuit, a very rich caramel sauce – delicious.Taste 7/10, Value 5/10, Originality 2/1062.Honeycomb andchocolate, Jude’s(460ml, £5.75, Ocado)This is a much nicer version of the flavours in the Crunchie ice-cream.Taste 6/10, Value 5/10, Originality 3/10View image in fullscreen“Much nicer version’ … Honeycomb & chocolate.Photograph: Jude’s61.Roasted strawberries, Brickell’s(475ml, £7.50, selected UK stores and online)Delicious real strawberry flavour – but the grainiest tub I tried.Taste 5/10, Value 4/10, Originality 5/1060.Trifle Twirl, M&S(500ml, £4.50, Ocado)A fun, Ben & Jerry’s-style loaded ice-cream (I haven’t included any Ben & Jerry’s tubs in this list because their flavours are all now mainstream). The sponge chunks are a bit too chewy.Taste 5/10, Value 5/10, Originality 4/1059.Heather honey, M&S(500ml, £5, Ocado)A really yummy, subtle, honey-flavoured ice-cream.Taste 7/10, Value 5/10, Originality 2/1058.Aunt Bessie’s yorkshire pudding,Anya Hindmarch(one scoop £4.50 or 500ml tub £16, The Ice Cream Project, London)This tastes more like pancakes with syrup than yorkshire puddings – but not in a bad way.Taste 7/10, Value 1/10, Originality 7/1057.Lemon curd, Norfolk County Dairy(500ml, £8.15, selected UK stores)A very subtle lemon flavour; I wasn’t getting curd specifically.Taste 5/10, Value 4/10, Originality 6/10View image in fullscreen‘Phish food on steroids’ … Jefferson’s Rockiest road.Photograph: Jefferson’s56.Rockiest road, Jefferson’s(370ml, £8.50, selected UK stores)Ben & Jerry’s phish food on steroids.Taste 7/10, Value 3/10, Originality 5/1055.Baileys vanilla, Carte D’Or(825ml, £4.50, Ocado)Baileys lovers will enjoy – does exactly what it says on the tub.Taste 4/10, Value 8/10, Originality 3/1054.Cornish honeycomb crunch, Kelly’s(950ml, £4, Iceland)There were nice crunchy bits of honeycomb on top, but it needed more throughout.Taste 5/10, Value 9/10, Originality 1/1053.Raspberry cheesecake withCornish clotted cream, Kelly’s(425ml, £4, Iceland)Way more delicious than I was expecting – the raspberry sauce is genuinely great.Taste 8/10, Value 5/10, Originality 2/1052.Golden syrup, Lyle’s(500ml, £4.75, Iceland)Incredibly sweet – but how could it not be?Taste 6/10, Value 5/10, Originality 4/10View image in fullscreen‘A bit underwhelming’ … Mango sticky rice.Photograph: James Moyle/Araw51.Mango sticky rice, Araw(475ml, £8, available for UK delivery)I wanted to love this vegan ice-cream, but the rice was still hard and the whole thing a bit underwhelming.Taste 3/10, Value 3/10, Originality 9/1050.Sicilian lemon and limoncello, Tesco(480ml, £3.50, Tesco)Inoffensive, but not tart enough.Taste 4/10, Value 5/10, Originality 6/1049-45.Ottolenghistrawberriesand cream with sumac/roasted pistachioand sour cherry/salted malted chocolate/coffee andcardamom/Madagascan vanillaand miso caramel,Waitrose(480ml tub, £6, Waitrose)I wanted more from all of these! More sumac, more sourness, more malt flavour …Taste 5/10, Value 5/10, Originality 6/1044.Dubai chocolate, Mister Twist(120ml, £5.50, selected UK stores)A fun, crunchy take on a trendy flavour.Taste 7/10, Value 2/10, Originality 7/10View image in fullscreen‘Fun and crunchy’ …  Dubai chocolate.Photograph: Siwan Jackson/Mister Twist43-40.Stem ginger and marmalade/Mini egg/Gingerbread/Cinnamon, SimplyIceCream(500ml, £6.50, available for UK delivery)All of these flavours from independent ice-cream maker Simply Ice Cream were lovely – but none of them blew my socks off.Taste 6/10, Value 5/10, Originality 5/1039.Matcha, Häagen-Dazs(460ml, £6, Waitrose)It’s easy to write off matcha as a zeitgeisty flavour, but in an ice-cream it’s undeniably refreshing.Taste 6/10, Value 5/10, Originality 6/1038.Irish coffee, SimplyIceCream(500ml, £6.50, available for UK delivery)I don’t love Irish coffees – but I was impressed by how much this tasted like one.Taste 5/10, Value 5/10, Originality 7/1037.Cinnamon bun, Waitrose(480ml, £3.50, Waitrose)Way too few chunks of bun – this felt like a missed opportunity! Artificial-tasting.Taste 4/10, Value 7/10, Originality 6/1036.Peach melba, Waitrose(480ml, £3.50, Waitrose)This nails the flavour of tinned peaches with sugary raspberry sauce.Taste 5/10, Value 7/10, Originality 5/1035-33.Basque cheesecake/Earl grey malted crumble/Ube halaya, Araw(475ml, £8, available for UK delivery)These felt like underwhelming representations of the unusual flavours they promised.Taste 5/10, Value 3/10, Originality 9/1032. Caramelised biscuit,Asda(425ml, £2.75, Asda)Layered with biscuit sauce, this might be even tastier than the official Lotus one.Taste 6/10, Value 7/10, Originality 4/1031.Flatwhite, M&S(500ml, £4.50, Ocado)More like an instant coffee than an espresso-based drink.Taste 5/10, Value 5/10, Originality 7/1030.Raspberry pavlova,Asda(900ml, £2.67 Asda)If you’re going to sell something as pavlova-flavoured, I think there should be more meringue chunks, but it’s cheap and relatively tasty.Taste 3/10, Value 9/10, Originality 5/1029.Tiramisu, Häagen-Dazs(420ml, £5.75, Tesco)It is my firm belief that no tiramisu-flavoured thing (and there are an increasing number of them) will ever be as good as actual tiramisu. This didn’t prove me wrong.Taste 5/10, Value 5/10, Originality 7/1028.Sicilian lemon meringue,Asda(500ml, £3.27, Asda)There were chunks of meringue throughout, and a lemon curd ripple – not bad.Taste 5/10, Value 6/10, Originality 6/10View image in fullscreenOn a quest to taste the best … Knight tries out a cornet with a twist.Photograph: Alicia Canter/The Guardian27.Mangolassi, Moonji(100ml, £3.49, selected UK stores and online)I was impressed that this vegan sorbet actually tasted like lassi, rather than just mango.Taste 7/10, Value 3/10, Originality 8/1026.Stem ginger, Salcombe Dairy(500ml, £6, Ocado)A creamy, gingery delight.Taste 9/10, Value 5/10, Originality 4/10View image in fullscreen“Creamy delight’ … Stem ginger.Photograph: Salcombe Dairy25.Matcha green tea, Jude’s(460ml, £5.75, Sainsbury’s)Slightly milder, and better, in my opinion, than Häagen-Dazs’s version.Taste 7/10, Value 5/10, Originality 6/1024.Fig leaf and currant jam, Milktooth Gelato(500ml, £9.50, selected UK stores)Earthy, interesting flavour – but some of the bits of currant were hard and gritty.Taste 5/10, Value 5/10, Originality 8/1023.Coconut kefir frozen yogurt, Waitrose(480ml, £3.50, Waitrose)There’s a lot going on here!
